title: Next-Generation Modulation and Control of Power Electronic Systems: AI-Enabled Control, Digital Twins, Fault-Tolerant Operation, and Cyber-Physical Security
content: Power electronic systems are evolving from conventional fixed-function converters toward intelligent, adaptive, and cyber-physical energy-conversion platforms in which modulation, predictive control, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DTs), fault diagnosis, and cybersecurity increasingly interact within a single closed-loop architecture. This paper presents an integrated review and unified mathematical framework for next-generation modulation and control of power electronic systems, with emphasis on advanced pulse-width and space-vector modulation, model predictive control (MPC), AI-assisted adaptation, DT-enabled monitoring, fault-tolerant operation, and cyber-resilient control. Unlike conventional reviews that address these technologies independently, the proposed framework links switched-converter dynamics, state and parameter estimation, residual-based diagnosis, physical faults, cyber disturbances, risk-adaptive control, and mode-dependent reconfiguration within a common formulation. The literature synthesis is complemented by an illustrative experimental case study that uses measured electrical machine operating data to evaluate the DT-based diagnostic and monitoring layers of the proposed architecture. Across five evaluated load conditions, the DT maintained a mean normalized root-mean-square error of 4.16%, with health indices remaining above 0.90, demonstrating consistent healthy-state tracking. Under representative injected sensor and torque-degradation scenarios, channel-specific residuals provided clear separation between healthy and abnormal conditions. AI-based residual classification achieved test accuracies above 97% across the evaluated classifiers, with the best-performing model reaching 98.61%. These experimentally grounded results support the feasibility of DT-assisted health assessment and intelligent diagnosis within the proposed cross-layer framework, while closed-loop integration of modulation, predictive control, fault-tolerant reconfiguration, and cyber-resilient operation remains an important direction for future experimental validation.
